items.stem: (a) Define a saturated solution? (b) Why is temperature strictly specified when defining the solubility of a substance? (c) A student dissolves 15 g of common salt in 85 g of water. Calculate the mass by mass percentage of the solution? (d) What happens if a saturated solution of a solid in liquid is heated?
items.answer: (a) A saturated solution is a solution in which no more solute can be dissolved in the solvent at a specific given temperature. (b) Temperature is strictly specified because the solubility of a solid solute in a liquid solvent generally increases as the temperature rises. Thus, a solution saturated at one temperature may become unsaturated when heated. (c) For the mathematical calculation: Mass of the solute (common salt) = 15 g Mass of the solvent (water) = 85 g Total mass of the solution = Mass of solute + Mass of solvent Total mass = 15 g + 85 g = 100 g Mass by mass percentage = (Mass of solute / Mass of solution) × 100 Mass by mass percentage = (15/100) × 100 = 15% (d) Heating a saturated solution increases its kinetic energy, allowing it to dissolve even more solute.

items.stem: (a) Draw a labelled diagram of the apparatus used to separate a mixture of acetone and water? (b) Explain the scientific principle behind this separation technique? (c) Why is this method highly suitable for separating acetone and water but not for separating crude petroleum components?
items.answer: (a) (b) The basic principle of simple distillation relies on a significant difference in the boiling points of two miscible liquids. The mixture is heated until the liquid with the lower boiling point vaporizes. These vapours travel into a condenser where they are cooled back into a liquid state and collected separately, leaving the higher boiling point liquid behind in the distillation flask. (c) This specific separation method is highly suitable for an acetone and water mixture because their boiling points differ by more than twenty-five degrees Celsius. Acetone boils at fifty-six degrees Celsius, while water boils at one hundred degrees Celsius. However, petroleum components have very closely spaced boiling points, usually differing by less than twenty-five degrees Celsius. Therefore, simple distillation fails to separate them purely, and complex fractional distillation must be used instead to isolate the petroleum fractions.

items.stem: (a) What is the Tyndall effect? (b) Why does a true homogeneous solution absolutely fail to show this visual effect? (c) Differentiate between a colloid and a suspension specifically based on particle size and settling behaviour? (d) Finally, identify the dispersed phase and dispersion medium in atmospheric clouds?
items.answer: (a) The Tyndall effect is the phenomenon where a beam of light becomes visible as it passes through a medium because the particles in that medium scatter the light. (b) A true solution does not exhibit this effect because its dissolved solute particles are incredibly small, measuring less than one nanometre in diameter, which is insufficient to scatter visible light waves. (c) A colloid differs from a suspension primarily in particle size and stability. Colloidal particles range between one and one thousand nanometres and remain uniformly distributed without settling down over time. In contrast, suspension particles are larger than one thousand nanometres and are unstable, settling down at the bottom due to gravity when left undisturbed. (d) In the specific case of clouds, the dispersed phase consists of liquid water droplets or solid ice crystals, while the dispersion medium is the surrounding gaseous air. items.stem: A sailor jumps out from a small boat to the shore (Fig). As the sailor jumps forward, will the boat move? If yes, in which direction and why.
items.answer: Yes, the boat will move backward, away from the shore. According to Newton’s third law of motion, as the sailor pushes the boat backward with their feet to jump forward, the boat exerts an equal and opposite force forward on the sailor. This backward force applied by the sailor causes the boat to move in the reverse direction.

items.stem: During a high jump event, a landing mat or sand bed is placed for the athlete to fall upon (Figure). Explain the reason behind it.
items.answer: The landing mat or sand bed provides a soft, compressible surface that increases the time it takes for the falling athlete to come to a complete stop. According to Newton’s second law of motion, force is equal to the rate of change of momentum. By extending the stopping time, the rate of change of momentum decreases, which significantly reduces the impact force exerted on the athlete’s body, thereby preventing serious injuries.

QUESTIONS: (a) What term describes the hot sugar syrup when it cannot dissolve any more sugar at that specific high temperature? items.answer: (a) The syrup is called a saturated solution at that specific temperature. (b) He was able to dissolve more sugar because the solubility of a solid solute in a liquid solvent generally increases with an increase in temperature. (c) As the syrup cooled overnight, the temperature dropped, causing the solubility of the sugar to decrease. The extra sugar that could no longer stay dissolved separated out from the solution as solid crystals.

items.answer: (a) It is a heterogeneous mixture of two immiscible liquids. (b) A separating funnel can be used to separate them. How Forces Affect Motion CHAPTER 6 How Forces Affect Motion SSummar 1. Force It is a push or pull. A force acting on a body changes or tries to change its state of rest or motion or changes the direction of motion. A force may start motion of an object, may change the speed of a moving object, may stop a moving object, may change the direction of an object or may deform an object. 2. Type of force The force is classified into two parts which is as follows : 1. Balanced forces : When two or more forces acting simultaneously on an object do not change its state of rest or of uniform linear motion, the forces are said to be balanced forces. The net resultant of all the balanced forces is zero. Balanced forces do not change the state of rest or of uniform linear motion of an object, but they can deform the object. 2. Unbalanced forces : When two or more forces acting simultaneously on an object change its state of rest or of uniform linear motion, the forces are said to be unbalanced forces. The net resultant of all the unbalanced forces is non-zero. 3. Galileo’s concept of motion Galileo, based on his experimental studies, concluded that objects move with a constant velocity if no external unbalanced force acts on them. On the other hand, net unbalanced external force not required to maintain uniform motion of an object along a straight line. Based on his experimental studies, Newton gave three fundamental laws which are called Newton’s laws of motion. 4. Newton’s first law of motion It states that an object remains in its state of rest or of uniform linear motion unless compelled by some external unbalanced force. Newton’s first law of motion defines force. Thus, force is an external effort, i.e., a push or a pull, which changes or tends to change the state of rest or of uniform linear motion of an object on which it acts. Newton’s first law of motion is also called the law of inertia. 5. Inertia It is inherent property of an object by virtue of which it resists any change in its state of rest or of uniform linear motion. Mass of an object is a measure of its inertia. Higher the mass of an object, larger is its inertia. 5.1 Types of Inertia Inertia is of three types : (i) inertia of rest, (ii) inertia of motion and (iii) inertia of direction. Dr. Ahmed runs a mobile clinic in a remote village with frequent power cuts. He needs to test blood samples for anemia by separating the heavier red blood cells from the lighter plasma. Since he cannot use an electric machine, he uses a ‘paperfuge’—a simple disk made of cardboard and string that he spins rapidly by pulling the strings. In another part of the village, a farmer is using a piece of alum (fitkari) to clean buckets of highly muddy river water, waiting for the fine dirt to clump and settle. QUESTIONS: (a) What is the separation technique Dr. Ahmed is imitating with his hand-powered paperfuge? (b) State the fundamental principle behind Dr. Ahmed’s separation technique. (c) According to the textbook, how is a blood mixture classified? (d) What is the scientific term for the process the farmer is using to clear the muddy water? (e) How exactly does the alum (fitkari) help in cleaning the farmer’s muddy water?
items.answer: (a) Dr. Ahmed is using centrifugation. (b) The principle is that when a mixture is spun rapidly, centrifugal force pushes the heavier particles to the bottom (or outward), while the lighter components remain at the top (or center). (c) Blood is classified as a colloid. (d) The process is called coagulation. (e) Alum acts as a coagulant. It causes the fine suspended mud particles, which would otherwise take a long time to settle, to clump together into larger, heavier masses that easily settle down at the bottom by gravity.

items.stem: A local dairy cooperative produces fresh paneer (cottage cheese) every morning. To make the paneer, workers heat large vats of fresh milk and add natural lemon juice. Almost immediately, the uniform liquid begins to separate into solid white curds and a watery, greenish-yellow liquid called whey. The heavy curds are then strained through a clean muslin cloth, pressed to remove excess water, and sold in blocks. QUESTIONS: (a) What scientific process occurs when lemon juice is added to the milk to form the curds? (b) What role does the lemon juice play in this process? (c) What separation technique is used when the workers pass the curd and whey mixture through the muslin cloth?
items.answer: (a) The process is called coagulation (specifically, the coagulation of milk proteins). (b) The lemon juice (which contains acid) acts as a coagulant, causing the proteins in the milk to clump together into larger solid masses (curds). (c) The separation technique used with the muslin cloth is filtration.
